name: Visa on Arrival (VoA)
summary: A 15-day tourist visa you buy at the airport or a designated border checkpoint for 2,000 THB. Since 15 September 2026 only three nationalities can use it: Azerbaijan, Belarus and Serbia. Everyone else either enters visa-free or needs a visa before travelling. India, China, Taiwan, Saudi Arabia and many former VoA countries have moved to visa exemption or a bilateral agreement, while others, such as Mexico, Uzbekistan and Armenia, now need an e-Visa.
seoTitle: Thailand Visa on Arrival 2026: 3 countries, 15 days, 2,000 THB
seoDescription: From 15 September 2026 Thailand's Visa on Arrival is only for Azerbaijan, Belarus and Serbia. Fee, 15-day stay, documents, funds and what former VoA countries must do now.
validity: Single entry. You may stay up to 15 days from the day you arrive (the arrival day counts as day 1).
extendableDetail: Immigration offices have historically allowed a short extension of a VoA stay (often up to 7 days, 1,900 THB) at the officer's discretion. Don't count on it: if you need longer than 15 days, get a tourist visa (TR) before you travel.
feeNote: 2,000 THB, paid in Thai baht cash at the VoA counter. Fees are non-refundable. Bring exact cash; exchange counters and ATMs are usually before the VoA desk but queues can be long.
financialRequirement: Show at least 10,000 THB per person or 20,000 THB per family in cash or equivalent.
processingTime: Issued at the counter on arrival, usually within 30 to 60 minutes, but queues at Suvarnabhumi and Don Mueang can be longer at peak times.
keyRequirements: A passport of Azerbaijan, Belarus or Serbia, valid for at least 6 months
Tourism only; no work of any kind
Arrival through a designated VoA checkpoint (main international airports and selected land borders)
A confirmed ticket leaving Thailand within 15 days
Cash for the 2,000 THB fee plus proof of at least 10,000 THB per person (20,000 THB per family)
A completed Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC)
documents: Passport valid for at least 6 months with a blank page
Completed VoA application form (available at the counter)
One recent passport photo, 4 x 6 cm
Confirmed return or onward ticket within 15 days
Hotel booking or address in Thailand for your stay
2,000 THB in cash for the fee
Proof of funds: at least 10,000 THB per person or 20,000 THB per family

howToApply.detail: Only Azerbaijani, Belarusian and Serbian passport holders can get a VoA from 15 September 2026. Other nationalities should check the exemption list or apply for an e-Visa.
Book a ticket out within 15 days, bring a passport photo, the fee in Thai baht cash and proof of funds, and submit your TDAC within 3 days before arrival.
After landing, follow the 'Visa on Arrival' signs before the immigration line. Hand in the form, photo, passport and fee.
Take your passport with the VoA sticker to the immigration counter for your entry stamp. Check the permitted-stay date.

bestFor: Short holidays of up to two weeks for Azerbaijani, Belarusian and Serbian travellers
Last-minute trips where there is no time to apply for an e-Visa
notFor: Trips longer than 15 days (apply for a tourist visa instead)
Nationalities other than Azerbaijan, Belarus and Serbia
commonMistakes: Relying on an old VoA list. Until September 2026 about 31 countries were eligible; now it is only three.
Arriving without Thai baht cash for the fee.
Forgetting a passport photo, which slows everything down.
Booking a return flight after day 15.
Entering at a land border that doesn't issue VoA.

faqs.q: Which countries can get a Visa on Arrival in Thailand now?
faqs.a: From 15 September 2026 only Azerbaijan, Belarus and Serbia. The previous list of about 31 countries no longer applies.

faqs.q: I'm Indian. Do I still need a Visa on Arrival?
faqs.a: No. From 15 September 2026, Indian passport holders are on the 30-day visa exemption list for tourism, so you can enter without a visa. Fill in the TDAC before arrival.

faqs.q: I'm from a former VoA country like Mexico, Uzbekistan or Armenia. What do I need?
faqs.a: These nationalities now need a visa before travelling. Apply for a tourist visa (TR) through the official Thai e-Visa website at least 2 to 4 weeks before your trip.

faqs.q: How much is the Visa on Arrival fee?
faqs.a: 2,000 THB, paid in cash in Thai baht at the VoA counter. It is non-refundable.

faqs.q: Can I extend a Visa on Arrival?
faqs.a: Sometimes, for a few days, at the officer's discretion at an immigration office. It isn't guaranteed. If you already know you'll stay longer than 15 days, get a tourist visa before you travel.

faqs.q: Do I need the TDAC with a Visa on Arrival?
faqs.a: Yes. All foreign arrivals must submit the Thailand Digital Arrival Card online within 3 days before arrival. It's free on tdac.immigration.go.th.
